extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians/counselors, organizational users, and individuals interested in assessing their humor style (adults and older adolescents)
extracted.subtask_description: Administer and score the Humor Styles Questionnaire (HSQ): a 32-item self-report instrument measuring four humor styles via 7-point Likert items, used in psychological research, counseling, and organizational settings. Includes item wording, response scale, scoring instructions (subscale sums with some reverse-scored items), and subscale interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliative (Subscale interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliative: High scores reflect frequent use of humor to build social bonds and ease interactions, supporting positive relationships and group cohesion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation guidance: Higher affiliative scores indicate frequent use of humor to create/maintain social relationships and reduce interpersonal tension. Use as one of four HSQ subscale scores when evaluating an individual's humor style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Enhancing (Subscale interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-Enhancing: High scores indicate a tendency to use humor to maintain a positive outlook and cope with stress, promoting personal psychological resilience and well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation guidance: Higher self-enhancing scores denote using humor internally to manage negative emotions and preserve a positive mood; consider this an adaptive coping indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive (Subscale interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggressive: High scores suggest a tendency to use humor at the expense of others (e.g., sarcasm, ridicule), which may harm relationships and is linked to negative psychosocial outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation guidance: Treat high aggressive scores as a potential risk factor for interpersonal problems; examples include teasing, sarcasm, or ridicule directed at others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Defeating (Subscale interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-Defeating: High scores show a pattern of using self-disparaging humor to gain approval or hide distress, often associated with lower self-esteem and poorer well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation guidance: High self-defeating scores indicate using self-deprecating jokes to ingratiate or mask problems; consider links to poorer psychological outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: HSQ items (32 Likert statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of 32 statements respondents rate (example items include: 'I usually don’t laugh or joke around much with other people.'; 'If I am feeling depressed, I can usually cheer myself up with humor.'; 'If someone makes a mistake, I will often tease them about it.'; ... 'Letting others laugh at me is my way of keeping my friends and family in good spirits.' ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration guidance: Present all 32 statements to respondents and collect one response per statement on the 7-point response scale. The page lists each item verbatim for use in surveys. Note: some items are reverse-scored when computing subscales (the page states 'with some items reverse scored').

rubrics_metrics.name: Response scale (Likert scoring values)
rubrics_metrics.description: Response options and numeric scoring: 'Totally disagree' = 1; 'Moderately disagree' = 2; 'Slightly disagree' = 3; 'Neither agree nor disagree' = 4; 'Slightly agree' = 5; 'Moderately agree' = 6; 'Totally agree' = 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this 1–7 numeric mapping to convert item responses into scores for summing into subscale totals. Ensure consistent mapping across all items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring method (subscale calculation and reverse scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: How is the HSQ scored? Each item is rated on a 7-point scale; subscale scores are calculated by summing relevant items, with some items reverse scored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring guidance: Identify which items belong to each of the four subscales (affiliative, self-enhancing, aggressive, self-defeating), apply reverse scoring to specified items, then sum the numeric item values to produce subscale totals. Compare totals across subscales and interpret using the subscale interpretation guidance above. (The template notes reverse-scoring but does not list which specific items are reverse-coded.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended population and settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility and typical uses: 'The Humor Styles Questionnaire can be completed by anyone interested in understanding their humor style.' The HSQ is suitable for adults and older adolescents and is commonly used in psychological research, counseling, and organizational settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use-case guidance: Administer to adults/older adolescents in research, clinical assessment, or organizational surveys. Consider the population when interpreting subscale scores and generalizing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference: Martin, R.A., Puhlik-Doris, P., Larsen, G., Gray, J., and Weir, K. (2003). Individual differences in uses of humor and their relation to psychological well-being: Development of the Humor Styles Questionnaire. Journal of Research in Personality, 37, 48-75. License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribution guidance: When using or distributing the HSQ template, cite the original paper (Martin et al., 2003) and honor the indicated CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license terms for reuse/modification in accordance with copyright requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated completion time
rubrics_metrics.description: Time to complete: '8 minutes to complete.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: Use this estimate for planning administration sessions and informing respondents about expected time commitment.
